title: Singing and the Bluebird reissue
summary: He sang only to fill a gap, is embarrassed by the reissue of early Bluebird sides, and learns Volume II was dropped when Frank Driggs left RCA.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Every so many, what, months, years. How about your singing? When did you start singing?

Well, I sang just because there wasn't anybody else to do it. We had a girl vocalist at times, but there was no -- at that time we couldn't afford a male vocalist, and so either I did it or one of the guys in the band would do it. It was just a questions of, you know, filling a gap. I never wanted to be a singer.
Because I know on some of the cuts on this Bluebird reissue --
Yes. I'm being internationally embarrassed with that. I thought those things were gone forever, but --
No, they find everything. The Complete Charlie Barnet, Volume I, 1935-1937, and the liner notes say you haven't heard anything yet. Volume II is what's really going to be something.
Unfortunately I hear there isn't going to be any Volume II. The guy that was doing this was replaced at RCA Victor and all of his projects along these lines were dropped.
I understand he's back now, but it's
very questionable how far they're going to let him go with that.
Oh, yeah. Gee, what a shame, because it was so great. They have all that material, and they're just gonna sit just sitting on it, right?
